problem.name: Discrete production scheduling
problem.statement_latex:
Given $J$ unit-time jobs, $M$ machines, due dates $d_j$, idle allowances $e_m$, production groups $P_{mj}$ and nonnegative costs $c_e,c_l,c_p$, choose distinct integer slots $t_{mj}\in\{1,\ldots,J+e_m\}$ for the jobs on each machine. Require $t_{m+1,j}\ge t_{mj}$ and that each machine's occupied slots form one consecutive interval. If $\pi_m(r)$ is its $r$th processed job, minimize
\[
c_e\sum_j(d_j-t_{Mj})_++c_l\sum_j(t_{Mj}-d_j)_+
+c_p\sum_{m=1}^{M}\sum_{r=1}^{J-1}\mathbf1[P_{m,\pi_m(r)}\ne P_{m,\pi_m(r+1)}],
\]
where $(a)_+=\max(a,0)$. This scheduling model captures delivery penalties and production-group changes in steel manufacturing. Complexity counts quantum gates and measurement samples and classical bit operations for the time-indexed binary formulation.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(KSpN)$ gates for hardware-efficient VQE and F-VQE; $O(KSp(N+q))$ for QAOA.
quantum.headline_text: $O(KSpN)$ gates for hardware-efficient VQE and F-VQE; $O(KSp(N+q))$ for QAOA.
quantum.details_latex: The time-indexed QUBO has $N=\sum_m J(J+e_m)+\sum_m e_m$ binary variables before presolving, and $q$ nonzero quadratic terms. Here $p$ counts circuit layers, $K$ counts primitive circuit evaluations and $S$ the shots per evaluation. A computational-basis sample gives a schedule assignment and its classically evaluated cost. VQE minimizes the sampled energy or a conditional-value-at-risk objective; filtering VQE (F-VQE) reweights sampled energies and uses parameter-shift updates. Variational imaginary-time evolution (VarQITE) uses the same state family and estimates a parameter metric: with $d$ parameters, a direct iteration needs $O(d^2+dq)$ measurement settings and an $O(d^3)$ classical linear-system solve. These settings contribute to $K$. QAOA uses phases for the QUBO terms and a transverse-field mixer. Parameter optimization and feasibility checks are part of the hybrid computation.

classical.headline_latex: $\min\{O^*(2^N),\operatorname{poly}(N,q,W)2^{\omega N/3},\operatorname{poly}(L)2^{O(L/\sqrt{\log L})}\}$, enumeration, weighted 2-CSP and exact threshold counting.
classical.headline_text: $\min\{O^*(2^N),\operatorname{poly}(N,q,W)2^{\omega N/3},\operatorname{poly}(L)2^{O(L/\sqrt{\log L})}\}$, enumeration, weighted 2-CSP and exact threshold counting.
classical.details_latex: Here $W$ bounds the integer QUBO score range after scaling, $\omega$ is the matrix-multiplication exponent, and $L$ is the size of a Boolean circuit checking the score threshold and constraints. These bounds apply to the same time-indexed instance, including its horizon and coefficient precision. Classical branch-and-bound, constraint programming and mixed-integer solvers use scheduling-specific propagation and lower bounds; their instance-dependent running times supply practical comparisons. The raw QUBO variable count can be reduced by fixing assignments and simplifying constraints before either classical or quantum optimization.

evidence.description_latex: The hardware experiments compare sampled energies and optimum frequencies on the tested instances; an asymptotic quantum speedup has not been established.

hardware.description_latex: Amaro et al. compared the four methods on a five-qubit instance and ran F-VQE on instances with up to 23 physical superconducting qubits after presolving. VQE, F-VQE and QAOA use $N$ data qubits; the Hadamard-test implementation of VarQITE adds an ancilla. Logical implementations must protect the complete repeated-measurement computation.
